200.body: Polish PM condemns “disgrace” of failed Venezuela oil deal under former government following FT report Sep 15, 2026 | Business , Law , Politics Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Prime Minister Donald Tusk says that Poland has been “disgraced in front of the entire world” by a new Financial Times report on how Polish state energy firm Orlen lost $230 million (856 million zloty) trying to buy Venezuelan oil through intermediaries, unsecured payments and cryptocurrency transfers. Orlen, which was under new management after Obajtek had been fired earlier that year following the arrival of Tusk’s government, said that the losses included around $240 million paid to a Dubai-based intermediary run by a 25-year-old from Hong Kong. 200.title: Polish foreign minister insists his country is not behind Hungary's blocking of Ukraine's EU accession
200.summary: Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski has insisted that Warsaw has nothing to do with Hungary blocking the opening of new clusters in Ukraine's EU accession negotiations. Source: Sikorski in an interview with European Pravda Details: Sikorski denied that Warsaw was in any way involved in the Hungarian government's decision to continue blocking the opening of further negotiating clusters for Ukraine.
200.body: Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski has insisted that Warsaw has nothing to do with Hungary blocking the opening of new clusters in Ukraine's EU accession negotiations. Source: Sikorski in an interview with European Pravda Details: Sikorski denied that Warsaw was in any way involved in the Hungarian government's decision to continue blocking the opening of further negotiating clusters for Ukraine. "There is a vigorous debate between Ukraine and the new Hungarian government on minority issues, and I hope it produces a positive result," the Polish foreign minister said. Background: Last week, the Council of the EU Working Party on Enlargement and Countries Negotiating Accession to the EU (COELA) failed to approve the results of the screening of negotiating clusters 2 and 3 for Ukraine because Hungary continued to block the decision.

(AFP) Europe Russia-Ukraine war Poland Poland's FM Radoslaw Sikorski Ukraine's FM Andriy Sybiga ERBIL (Kurdistan24) - Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski has warned that NATO could defeat Russia relatively quickly if Moscow directly attacked the alliance, arguing that NATO's overwhelming air superiority would make such a confrontation extraordinarily costly for the Kremlin. "If Russia attacked us and we took our gloves off, I think we would defeat Russia quite quickly," Sikorski said, according to a report by Kyiv Post journalist Alisa Orlova.
